summary.plain: In 1978 the PLUTO experiment at DESY's DORIS ring reported a narrow resonance at 9.46 GeV formed in e+e- annihilation. This is the Upsilon, a bound state of a bottom quark and its antiquark, first seen at Fermilab in 1977.
summary.technical: PLUTO at DORIS: narrow resonance at 9.46 GeV in e⁺e⁻ annihilation (Phys. Lett. B 76 (1978) 243-245); the Υ had been discovered in hadron collisions at Fermilab in 1977; DORIS was upgraded to reach it.

title: Observation of a narrow resonance formed in e+e− annihilation at 9.46 GeV
why_it_matters: Ziemann notes that the Upsilon, a bound state of two bottom quarks, was discovered at Fermilab in 1977 and that DORIS was upgraded to energies where Upsilons could be produced.
